title: A small circle carved in stone

probes.question: What symbol for zero appears on the Gwalior inscription?
True or false: the Bakhshali manuscript is described as a practical manual on arithmetic for merchants.

image.alt: A sandstone slab carved with five tally marks followed by a hollow circle, with an orange sun disc behind its top-right corner.

panels.text: The first known use of special glyphs for the decimal digits that includes the indubitable appearance of a symbol for the digit zero, a small circle, is on a stone inscription at the Chaturbhuj Temple, Gwalior, in India.
A symbol for zero, a black dot, is used throughout the Bakhshali manuscript, a practical manual on arithmetic for merchants.
The Bodleian Library reported radiocarbon dating results for six folios of the manuscript, indicating that they came from different centuries.
